messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have a direct way to calculate the freezing point of water at a given pressure. However, I can provide you with an estimate based on the standard phase diagram of water.

At a pressure of **10 kPa** (which is well above the triple‑point pressure of 611 Pa), water will freeze at a temperature slightly below its normal freezing point of 0 °C. The melting/freezing point of ice I at this pressure is approximately:

| Pressure | Freezing / Melting Point |
|----------|--------------------------|
| 10 kPa   | –2.9 °C (≈ –3 °C)        |

So, at 10 kPa, water freezes at roughly **–3 °C**. If you’d like to see how the boiling point changes at this pressure, I can use the available tool to calculate that for you.
